summary.intent: Review a subagent's perf branch (`perf/convert-single-flight`) that adds single-flight deduplication to conversions, checking its soundness before the change is accepted or merged.
summary.outcome: The subagent reported the branch as done: duplicate conversions eliminated, output identical to main, tests and checks passing. The assistant started a close diff review, focusing on whether one walk can wait on multiple flights, but had not reached a verdict by the end of the transcript.

repo: Single-flight conversion tracks waits with a `waiting` map holding a single edge per walk. Deadlock detection by cycle check is only sound if a walk never waits on more than one flight at once.
The deadlock test hangs and fails if the cycle check is removed, and the request-count test fails with flights off, so both guard the feature.
PR #509 is already on main and probably explains why the CPU gain on Chakra (10.1 → 9.3 s) is much smaller than Codex's 27%.
Conversion work is in `crates/semantic`; the session touched `kept.rs` and `lib.rs`.
Verification includes a lint gate, nextest and `test-checker-lane`.
